source.title_on_document: Expandora: Broadening Design Exploration with Text-to-Image Model

supplement.where: Appendix A, pp. 7-8; Appendices B-C, p. 8 and Tables 1-2 on p. 9; Appendix D, p. 8 and Figure 3 on p. 10 of this PDF.
supplement.holds: Prompt templates (Appendix A); participant details (Appendix B, Table 1); survey wording and complete survey means, standard deviations, and p-values, including the aggregated CSI statistics absent from the main text (Appendix C, Table 2); generated-image examples (Appendix D, Figure 3).

paper_design_summary: A formative study recruited six design students or graduates for a 40-minute mascot-design session using unspecified image generation models, followed by a 15-minute interview about difficulties in design exploration (pp. 2-3, Section 3). A subsequent within-subjects evaluation had eight participants complete a 25-minute mascot-design task with Expandora and another with ChatGPT image generation; system and topic order was counterbalanced (pp. 4-5, Section 5). The evaluation compared prompt counts, average semantic similarity between prompts (comparison set and aggregation not stated), and self-reported creativity support and workload; no scored image-creativity outcome is reported (p. 5, Sections 6-6.2; pp. 8-10, Appendices C-D).

studies.label: User study: Expandora vs ChatGPT image generation (within-subjects, N=8)

assignment.what_was_assigned: Order of the two systems (Expandora, ChatGPT baseline) and of the two design topics; every participant used both systems
assignment.quote: The order of topics and systems used was counterbalanced across participants.

arms.name: Expandora
arms.description: Structured input (part of prompt, add details or generate alternatives, novelty level); GPT-4o prompt suggestions; DALL-E 2 images; mindmap interface

arms.name: Baseline (ChatGPT)
arms.description: ChatGPT with an image generation feature

participants.who: 8 participants familiar with graphic design and the T2I model, with prior experience in three design projects and regular image-generation use. Section 5 reports 6 females and 2 males, age M=23.75 and SD=1.67 (p. 4). Table 1 instead labels P1-P6 and P8 Female and P7 Male (p. 9); the sex breakdown is internally inconsistent and cannot be resolved from this PDF. Student or professional status is not stated.
participants.quote: We conducted a within-subjects comparative study (N=8) to assess the effectiveness of Expandora in supporting design exploration using the T2I model.

ai_tool.name_model: Expandora (GPT-4o prompt suggestions, OpenAI DALL-E 2 images) vs ChatGPT with image generation
ai_tool.how_used: Participants entered prompts to generate reference images; Expandora proposed four prompt variations at a chosen novelty level and showed history as a mindmap; the baseline was ChatGPT image generation

task.description: Explore concepts for a mascot character: (1) a multi-genre music festival with an exotic vibe, (2) a laboratory researching cutting-edge future technology
task.duration: 25 minutes per task, after a 5-minute tutorial; 15-minute interview after both sessions

outcomes.name: Average semantic similarity between prompts (prompt diversity)
outcomes.measure_detail: Average semantic similarity between prompts used to generate images; the authors interpret lower similarity as more diverse prompts. The similarity function/model, use of embeddings, prompt comparison set (within or across participants), aggregation, and analysis unit are not stated (p. 5, Section 6.2). Section 6 names a two-sample paired t-test for usage logs without defining those details. The BERT model in Section 4.2.1 scores word concreteness and is not identified as the model for this outcome. Construct, question, measure, and unit are null because flexibility versus across-person diversity, with_ai versus across_people, an embedding-based method, and participant-level analysis cannot be confirmed.

contrasts.reported: Expandora M=0.476, SD=0.10 vs baseline M=0.666, SD=0.10; p=0.0032 (paired t-test; evaluation sample N=8; number of similarity observations not stated)
contrasts.locator: p. 5, Section 6.2; usage-log test named in Section 6; evaluation N=8 in p. 4, Section 5

outcomes.name: Number of prompts tried in 25 minutes
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Count of prompts tested, from usage logs

contrasts.reported: Expandora M=30.88, SD=9.16 vs baseline M=14, SD=4.72; p=0.0007 (paired t-test, N=8)
contrasts.locator: p. 5, Section 6.1; test named in Section 6

outcomes.name: Aggregated Creativity Support Index (self-report)
outcomes.question: none
outcomes.measure_detail: Aggregated CSI on a 7-point scale; Wilcoxon signed-rank test

contrasts.reported: Aggregated CSI: baseline M 5.06, STD 0.81; Expandora M 5.53, STD 0.80; P 0.383

studies.label: Formative study (six recruited, before system development)

assignment.what_was_assigned: A formative mascot-design session using image generation models is described; no allocation to AI comparison conditions is reported (pp. 2-3, Section 3).
assignment.quote: Participants were asked to brainstorm about the mascot character design for their company (for practitioners) or department (for students) using image generation models for a 40-minute session.

arms.name: Formative T2I exploration
arms.description: Mascot-design exploration using unspecified image generation models, with participants explaining intentions and reflecting on the images; no comparison condition is described (p. 3, Section 3).

participants.exclusions: Not stated; six were recruited, but a separate analyzed or post-exclusion count is not reported (pp. 2-3, Section 3).
participants.who: Six design students or graduates with experience in at least three graphic design projects were recruited. The text describes mascot design for a company (practitioners) or department (students), without a breakdown of participant status (pp. 2-3, Section 3).
participants.quote: we conducted a formative study with 6 participants to investigate the challenges of using T2I models during exploration

ai_tool.name_model: Text-to-image models; specific names and versions not stated (pp. 2-3, Section 3).
ai_tool.how_used: Participants generated mascot images, explained their intentions and expectations for each prompt, and reflected on whether generated images matched those intentions (p. 3, Section 3).

task.description: Brainstorm a mascot character for the participant's company or department; the session and interview examined difficulties in design exploration. Findings are qualitative, with no scored creativity or diversity outcome reported (pp. 2-3, Sections 3-3.1).
task.duration: 40-minute session followed by a 15-minute semi-structured interview (p. 3, Section 3).

sample_overlap.shares_participants_with: Not stated whether the formative study (S2) and comparative evaluation (S1) share participants; no combined unique-person total is recorded.

company_involvement.description: Coauthor Hyunjoon Jung is affiliated with Adobe, San Jose, CA, United States.

eligibility.reason: The comparative evaluation includes 8 participants (p. 4, Section 5; p. 9, Table 1), and the formative study recruited six (pp. 2-3, Section 3); neither meets the 50-person criterion. The evaluation counterbalances system and topic order without stating randomization (p. 5, Section 5); the formative study reports no AI comparison conditions (pp. 2-3, Section 3). Only prompt counts, prompt similarity, and survey outcomes are quantified in the evaluation; the similarity comparison set and aggregation are unspecified, and no scored image-creativity or confirmed across-person diversity outcome is reported, leaving criterion 3 unclear (p. 5, Sections 6-6.2; pp. 8-10, Appendices C-D). Neither study supplies an AI-versus-human output comparison, a qualifying observational comparison, or a synthesis, so context_class remains none.

one_line_finding: With Expandora, the 8 participants tried more prompts (M=30.88 vs 14, p=0.0007) with lower average semantic similarity (0.476 vs 0.666, p=0.0032) than with ChatGPT image generation, and the aggregated Creativity Support Index did not differ (5.53 vs 5.06, p=0.383) (p. 5; Table 2, p. 9).
open_questions: Which similarity model and function were used, which prompt pairs were compared, and how were scores aggregated into the observations analyzed? These details are not stated (p. 5, Sections 6 and 6.2; pp. 7-10, Appendices A-D).
Which sex breakdown is correct: the 6 females and 2 males in Section 5 (p. 4), or the Table 1 labels P1-P6 and P8 Female, P7 Male (p. 9)?

Did the six-person formative study and eight-person evaluation share participants, and how many formative participants were analyzed? No overlap or separate formative analyzed count is stated (pp. 2-3, Section 3; pp. 4-5, Section 5).
